source.title: Who Is Your Right Mixup Partner in Positive and Unlabeled Learning?

scope: Source-audit anchors only. Not a new experimental result, numeric verdict, admission, or addition to the frozen survey comparison matrix.

project_protocol_comparison.scope: Read-only comparability audit against the frozen Pilot protocol and its indexed CIFAR-10 split manifests. This is not a new experiment, protocol amendment, comparison-matrix entry, or numeric verdict.

image_backbones.native_cnn: ResNet-18 small-input stem, end-to-end, random initialization

assessment.CIFAR-10-1_positive_mapping: matches the frozen Pilot positive class definition
assessment.CIFAR-10-2_positive_mapping: complementary to the frozen Pilot; not the same positive-label task
assessment.fixed_positive_budget: does_not_match: paper reports 1000 labeled positives; Pilot SCAR counts vary with c
assessment.validation_and_selection: does_not_match_or_cannot_be_aligned: paper reports 500 validation instances without sampling frame, class composition, or selection use; Pilot has separate 2500-row pu_val and clean_val roles and explicit PA/OA selection
assessment.backbone_and_preprocessing: does_not_match: paper reports a 7-layer CNN; Pilot uses end-to-end or frozen random ResNet-18, train-only channel statistics, and no augmentation
assessment.repeats: both report/use five runs or seeds, but paper does not bind them to the Pilot split identities

caveats: Repeated E/C values in Tables 2 and 3 are duplicate reports in the same paper, not independent experiments.

Section 3.1 reports 500 validation instances but does not specify their sampling frame, class composition, or how they are used for model/parameter selection; do not infer these from the reported accuracy tables.
These anchors do not establish comparability with the toolbox ResNet-18 pilot: backbone, split construction, selection rule, and full training recipe differ or remain unresolved.
Table 2 baseline rows are source-reported comparisons; Appendix A is referenced for implementation details, but the table alone does not establish exact source-code reproduction by this project.

The two Supervised rows are non-PU full-supervision references. Their label/sample budget is not sufficiently documented for matched-budget comparison; do not treat them as PU-method anchors or as the project PN oracle result.
The paper reports five independent runs but does not provide per-run observations, so seed-level values cannot be reconstructed from mean and standard deviation.
